name: Low Earth Orbit (LEO)
info: Circular 400 km altitude with 51.6° inclination. Rapid 92-minute orbital period, moderate radiation, frequent Earth ground station passes.

name: Sun-Synchronous Polar Orbit (SSO)
info: Circular 705 km polar orbit with 98.2° inclination. Consistent solar illumination angle across daytime passes, optimal for Earth climate and land-cover imaging.

name: Geostationary Transfer Orbit (GTO)
info: Highly eccentric elliptical orbit with 250 km perigee and 35,786 km apogee. Gateway trajectory requiring onboard propulsion for orbit circularization or planetary escape.

name: Geostationary Earth Orbit (GEO)
info: Circular equatorial orbit at 35,786 km altitude matching Earth's rotational period. Spacecraft remains stationary over a fixed longitude, ideal for continuous weather tracking.

name: Low Lunar Orbit (LLO - Moon)
info: Circular 100 km polar orbit around the Moon. Direct overhead access to permanently shadowed lunar south pole craters; requires orbital stationkeeping against mascon gravity anomalies.

name: Low Mars Science Orbit (Mars)
info: Sun-synchronous 300 km science orbit around Mars. Solar irradiance drops to 43% of Earth levels (1.524 AU); deep space radio signals experience 4 to 21 minute round-trip light time.
